correctness.rationale: An independent exact reconstruction found 17 vertices, 68 edges, 68 triangles, no tetrahedra and a rank-bound 52×52 boundary minor of determinant −1. The edges of gap one give connectedness and rank 16 for ∂1. The unit minor makes im ∂2 primitive of rank 52, hence equal to ker ∂1, and ker ∂2 is free of rank 16. The independent cycle basis has integral entries and a free-coordinate identity; the translation norm vanishes and the first sixteen translates of the first cycle have determinant −1. Multiplication by t−1 identifies the resulting cyclic quotient with the translation augmentation ideal. All 136 signed affine traces match fixed vertices minus one. In particular an affine involution is conjugate to negation, which exchanges endpoints on four invariant edges and exchanges two vertices on four invariant triangles, so the two signs cancel in the Lefschetz trace. Other nontranslation affine maps have just one fixed vertex and no invariant edges or triangles. The rational restriction to translations is cyclotomic irreducible, and the two size-eight orbits of nontrivial characters are exchanged by a nonsquare Galois automorphism but not by complex conjugation (−1 is square).
residual_risks: This is exact finite evidence for Paley-17, not a formal proof assistant certificate or an integral classification for the full affine group.

Also, over C the restriction has each nontrivial character exactly once and the square multiplier acts freely on each of its two orbits. Choosing one weight vector and its multiplier translates in each orbit forces the affine representation, with no extra extension choice. Thus even the existence of a cyclic integral basis is covered by the prior facts, independently of the same-day rational overlap.
